newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-National Mutual shares list at A$1.75.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-National Mutual shares list at A$1.75.

text.p: The shares of Australian life office, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, on Tuesday debuted at A$1.75, a 15 cents or 9.4 percent premium to the group's institutional subscription price of A$1.60 per share.

The group's share institutional share offer closed six times oversubscribed last week and the final price of A$1.60 per share was higher than indicative bidding range of A$1.35 to A$1.55 initially set for institutions.
At 0155 GMT, National Mutual shares were trading at A$1.78, giving the Australia's second biggest life office a market capitalisation of about A$3.0 billion.
National Mutual is owned 51 percent by insurance and financial services giant Axa SA, which is prevented under the terms of the float from selling down its stake for six months after the listing.
Axa effectively bought into National Mutual last year at around A$1.25 per share.
Under the float, National Mutual's 1.2 million policy-holders were offered either shares or a cash alternative.
About 448 million shares not taken up by the policy-holders were then offered to retail investors and institutions.
Retail investors were offered the shares at A$1.50 each in September before the final price was set at the close of institutional bidding on September 27.
Dealers said the premium for National Mutual stock on listing reflected the large number of institutional bidders which failed to secure enough shares in the offer.
Analysts had estimated institutions received on average only about 15 percent of the allotments sought in the price-setting institutional component of the offer.

National Mutual's listing completes its 21-month transition from a mutual company owned by its policy-holders to a listed group free to pursue its strategic focus on Asia, unshackled by a mutual requirement to act solely in policy-holders' interests.
